entries.heading: Verse 1
entries.text: 1Sa 11:1-4 . Nahash Offers Them of Jabesh-gilead a Reproachful Condition.

entries.heading: 2. thrust out all your right eyes
entries.text: 2. thrust out all your right eyes --literally, "scoop" or "hollow out" the ball. This barbarous mutilation is the usual punishment of usurpers in the East, inflicted on chiefs; sometimes, also, even in modern history, on the whole male population of a town. Nahash meant to keep the Jabeshites useful as tributaries, whence he did not wish to render them wholly blind, but only to deprive them of their right eye, which would disqualify them for war. Besides, his object was, through the people of Jabesh-gilead, to insult the Israelitish nation.

entries.heading: 3, 4. send messengers unto all the coasts of Israel
entries.text: 3, 4. send messengers unto all the coasts of Israel --a curious proof of the general dissatisfaction that prevailed as to the appointment of Saul. Those Gileadites deemed him capable neither of advising nor succoring them; and even in his own town the appeal was made to the people--not to the prince.

entries.heading: Verse 5
entries.text: 1Sa 11:5-11 . They Send to Saul, and Are Delivered.

entries.heading: 7. he took a yoke of oxen, and hewed them in pieces
entries.text: 7. he took a yoke of oxen, and hewed them in pieces --(see Jud 19:29 ). This particular form of war-summons was suited to the character and habits of an agricultural and pastoral people. Solemn in itself, the denunciation that accompanied it carried a terrible threat to those that neglected to obey it. Saul conjoins the name of Samuel with his own, to lend the greater influence to the measure, and to strike greater terror unto all contemners of the order. The small contingent furnished by Judah suggests that the disaffection to Saul was strongest in that tribe.

entries.heading: 8. Bezek
entries.text: 8. Bezek --This place of general muster was not far from Shechem, on the road to Beth-shan, and nearly opposite the ford for crossing to Jabesh-gilead. The great number on the muster-roll showed the effect of Saul's wisdom and promptitude.

entries.heading: 11. on the morrow, that Saul put the people in three companies
entries.text: 11. on the morrow, that Saul put the people in three companies --Crossing the Jordan in the evening, Saul marched his army all night, and came at daybreak on the camp of the Ammonites, who were surprised in three different parts, and totally routed. This happened before the seven days' truce expired.
